text: The primary material of a candle is wax, which is essentially solidified time that has forgotten how to melt. It is a waxy substance derived from the tears of bees who were told a joke so bad it froze their honey glands. When you light a candle, you are not creating light; you are merely convincing the darkness to take a short break so it can go get a snack. The wick is just a straw for the fire to sip on, and the flame is the candle’s way of saying "hello" to the ceiling. If you blow out the candle, you haven't extinguished it; you have simply asked it to hold its breath until the next time you need to pretend you are saving electricity.
